title: Principal-adic lifting from a conormal nullhomotopy
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $a\in A$, $q\geq0$, and $R=\widehat{A[t_1,\ldots,t_q]}_{(a)}/L$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], where $L$ is an ideal and $R$ is $(a)$-adically complete. Let $\delta_R:L/L^2\to R^{\oplus q}$ send $g\bmod L^2$ to $(\partial g/\partial t_i\bmod L)_i$, with continuous derivatives. Suppose $h\geq0$ and an $R$-linear map $H:R^{\oplus q}\to L/L^2$ satisfy $\delta_RH=a^h\mathrm{id}_{R^{\oplus q}}$ and $H\delta_R=a^h\mathrm{id}_{L/L^2}$. Let $T$ be a commutative $(a)$-adically complete $A$-algebra and $t\geq0$ such that $T[a^\infty]\cap a^tT=0$, where $T[a^\infty]=\{x\in T:\text{there is }k\geq0\text{ with }a^kx=0\}$. For every integer $n>\max(2h,h+t)$ and every $A$-algebra map $\psi_n:R\to T/a^nT$, there is an $A$-algebra map $\varphi:R\to T$ whose reduction modulo $a^{n-h}T$ equals the reduction of $\psi_n$ modulo $a^{n-h}T$.

source.place: Tag 0AK7 (lemma-get-morphism-principal), with its Ext-annihilation hypothesis specialized to the displayed nullhomotopy of the completed two-term conormal complex (equation-NL).

proof.text: Write $P=\widehat{A[t_1,\ldots,t_q]}_{(a)}$. We first improve any map $\psi_m:R\to T/a^mT$ with $m>\max(2h,h+t)$. Put $s=m-h$, so $s\geq1$, $s>t$, and $2s>m$. Set $M=a^mT/a^{2m}T$, $Q=a^sT/a^{2m-h}T$, and $N=a^sT/a^{2s}T$. All three are annihilated by $a^m$, so they are $R$-modules through $\psi_m$. Multiplication by $a^h$ defines an $R$-linear bijection $\mu:Q\to M$. Indeed it is surjective since $a^mT=a^h a^sT$. If $x\in a^sT$ and $a^hx=a^{2m}z$, then $x-a^{2m-h}z$ lies in $a^sT$ and is killed by $a^h$. It is zero since $s\geq t$ and $T[a^\infty]\cap a^tT=0$. This proves injectivity. This calculation replaces the nonzerodivisor assumption in Tag 0AK6 by the bounded-torsion hypothesis of Tag 0AK7.

source.place: Tags 0AK6 (lemma-get-morphism-nonzerodivisor), first paragraph, and 0AK7 (lemma-get-morphism-principal); explicit high-ideal division calculation.

proof.text: Choose $y_i\in T$ lifting $\psi_m(\bar t_i)$. By [lem-per-completed-polynomial-taylor-evaluation], the tuple defines an evaluation $E_y:P\to T$. Its reduction modulo $a^m$ equals the composite $P\to R\xrightarrow{\psi_m}T/a^mT$: both are continuous $A$-algebra maps with the same coordinates, so the uniqueness clause applies. Here every $A$-algebra map preserves powers of $(a)$ and hence is continuous; $T/a^mT$ is complete because its quotient tower is eventually constant. Consequently $E_y(L)\subseteq a^mT$.

source.place: Tags 0AJM (formal-spaces.tex, remark-universal-property) and 0GAP (remark-improve-homomorphism), choice of a lift of the polynomial coordinates.

proof.text: Define $o:L/L^2\to M$ by $o([g])=E_y(g)\bmod a^{2m}T$. This is well-defined since $E_y(L^2)\subseteq a^{2m}T$. For $p\in P$ and $g\in L$, the equality $E_y(pg)=E_y(p)E_y(g)$ shows $R$-linearity: the scalar $p\bmod L$ acts through $E_y(p)\bmod a^mT=\psi_m(p\bmod L)$. Put $\beta=oH:R^{\oplus q}\to M$. The assumed equality $H\delta_R=a^h\mathrm{id}$ gives $\beta\delta_R=a^ho$. No Ext identification or obstruction-existence theorem is being invoked here; $o$ is the displayed map on representatives.

source.place: Tag 0GAP (remark-improve-homomorphism), the displayed map o(psi); direct use of the given conormal nullhomotopy.

proof.text:
Let $\pi:Q\to N$ be reduction and $j:M\to N$ the map induced by inclusion $a^mT\subseteq a^sT$. Both are well-defined since $2m-h\geq2s$ and $2m\geq2s$. Put $c=\pi\mu^{-1}\beta:R^{\oplus q}\to N$. For every $x\in a^mT$, viewing $x$ also in $Q$ gives $\mu([x]_Q)=[a^hx]_M$; hence $\pi\mu^{-1}(a^h[x]_M)=j([x]_M)$. It follows that $c\delta_R=jo$. Choose $d_i\in a^sT$ representing $c(e_i)$. For every $g\in L$, this equality reads
$$E_y(g)\equiv\sum_i E_y(\partial_i g)d_i\pmod{a^{2s}T}.$$
Indeed the coordinates of $\delta_R[g]$ are $\partial_i g\bmod L$ and their actions on $N$ are through $\psi_m$, equivalently through $E_y$. Changing a representative of such a scalar by $a^mT$ changes its product with $d_i$ by $a^{m+s}T\subseteq a^{2s}T$.

source.place: Tags 0AK6 and 0GAP, factoring the included error map through the conormal differential; explicit division and representative calculation.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-completed-polynomial-taylor-evaluation] with coordinate increment $(-d_i)_i\in(a^sT)^q$. For every $g\in L$ it gives
$$E_{y-d}(g)\equiv E_y(g)-\sum_i E_y(\partial_i g)d_i\equiv0\pmod{a^{2s}T}.$$
Thus $E_{y-d}$ factors through an $A$-algebra map $\psi_{2s}:R\to T/a^{2s}T$. The same lemma gives $E_{y-d}(f)\equiv E_y(f)\pmod{a^sT}$ for every $f\in P$, so $\psi_{2s}$ and $\psi_m$ agree modulo $a^sT$. This proves the required one-step improvement from precision $m$ to precision $2(m-h)$, with agreement at precision $m-h$.

source.place: Tags 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation), 0GAP (remark-improve-homomorphism), correction of coordinates, and 0AK6, improvement of precision.

proof.text: Starting with $m_0=n$ and $\psi^0=\psi_n$, repeat steps 1--5 recursively, putting $m_{j+1}=2(m_j-h)$ and choosing $\psi^{j+1}$ given there. The formula $m_j=2h+2^j(n-2h)$ proves that $m_j$ increases without bound, so every $m_j>\max(2h,h+t)$ and the construction remains applicable. Write $s_j=m_j-h$. For every $j$, $\psi^{j+1}$ and $\psi^j$ agree modulo $a^{s_j}T$, while $s_{j+1}>s_j$ and $s_j$ tends to infinity. For any $k\geq0$ define $f_k:R\to T/a^kT$ by reducing $\psi^j$ for any $j$ with $s_j\geq k$. Consecutive choices agree by the preceding congruence, and therefore all such choices agree. Reducing $f_{k+1}$ gives $f_k$ by choosing the same sufficiently large $j$.

source.place: Tag 0AK6 (lemma-get-morphism-nonzerodivisor), second paragraph; explicit recurrence and compatible reductions.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], the compatible family $(f_k)_k$ defines $r\mapsto(f_k(r))_k$ from $R$ to $\varprojlim_k T/a^kT$, with addition, multiplication, unit and $A$-scalar compatibility checked coordinatewise. Completeness identifies this ring with $T$ by the inverse of the canonical $A$-algebra map. Composing gives $\varphi:R\to T$. At $k=s_0=n-h$ one may choose $j=0$, so the reduction of $\varphi$ is $f_{n-h}=\psi_n\bmod a^{n-h}T$, as asserted.

source.place: Tag 0AK6, final paragraph; algebra.tex Section 00M9 and Definition 0317, inverse-limit definition of completion.
